text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites, and articles. Users can improve results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are good at tasks like answering questions, summarising texts, and translating languages. However, they also have limits. They may produce incorrect information, reflect biases in their training data, and cannot truly understand meaning the way humans do.
